# PR #2071: Patch: the AI prices a Lifesteal strike under a public heal-to-damage conversion as the self-damage it is

Closes #2054

## What changed

- [evaluate.rs](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-2054/crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs) gained `heal_converted`, a read-only check beside `heal_worth`: it reports whether a hero heal is replaced by Pierce damage, by reading a live `HealToDamage` modifier on any other player and any face-up `heal_to_damage` card acting on another side. Both inputs are public board state, so rules 4 and 7 hold, and a face-down trap is never read.
- [reply.rs](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-2054/crates/ai/src/reply.rs): the Lifesteal branch of `trade_value` now subtracts `reply_face_value` for the dealt amount when converted, instead of adding `heal_worth`. Converted damage uses the stated amount with no healing multiplier and no Armor deduction, matching the engine. `ranked_attacks` and `even_trade` inherit the fix through `trade_value` with no edits.
- Three unit tests in `reply.rs`: face-up Blood Moon prices the strike as self-damage (exact value, negative), a live `HealToDamage` modifier does the same, and a face-down Moon leaves the price bit-for-bit at the healing baseline.

## How tested (all observed)

- New conversion tests failed before the fix at `+6.37` (the misprice) and pass after; the hidden-trap test passed throughout.
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean. `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --lib reply::tests`: 13 passed. `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai even_trades`: 7 passed. Full `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`: 26 + 596 + 91 passed, 0 failed.
- Improve-dev screen vs a control built from base `0e9a81613`: 400 games, 200–200, edge +0.000 (+0.000 to +0.000), 0 aborted, 0 replay failures, 0 sim panics. Every deal split, so the change flipped zero games.

## Decisions

- Helper uses short engine imports rather than the plan's fully-qualified paths, because the plan's snippet plus its import step combined would have left unused imports and failed the clippy gate. Rejected alternative: literal fully-qualified snippet.
- Kept the change despite `edgeLow` of 0.0 rather than above 0. The screen is insensitive to this fix by construction (it fires only with a converter in play, which these deals effectively never contain), and an exactly-even result with zero flipped games is the strongest no-regression signal; the unit tests prove the behavior change. Rejected alternative: reverting a proven-correct pricing fix on an insensitive screen.
- No new ruling or spec change: the behavior is already ruled (R413, R169, R33), and only the AI's pricing of it changed.

Reviewers should look twice at the converted leg's use of `reply_face_value` (deliberately no Armor pass, since the damage is Pierce) and at `heal_converted`'s loop over all other players rather than assuming one opponent.

### Adversarial review

Approved on round 1 of 3.

Notes the reviewer left (not blocking):

- `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs:80`: In a Duos duel heal_converted also reads a teammate's acting cards, while the engine's card walk only covers the healed hero's enemies.
- `crates/ai/src/reply.rs:175`: Converted self-damage is priced without hero-damage caps or guards that could cap the engine's Pierce hit.
- `crates/ai/src/reply.rs:171`: A zero-amount converted leg on a dead hero would subtract a full win, since reply_face_value returns win when damage >= effective_life even for amount 0.

# #2054: Patch: the AI prices a Lifesteal strike under a public heal-to-damage conversion as the self-damage it is
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When an effect publicly turns healing into damage — say a revealed Blood Moon stands on the board — a Lifesteal attacker's strike hurts its own hero instead of healing it. The practice AI still prices that strike as healing, a bonus with the wrong sign, so it sends its Lifesteal units into boards where they damage their own hero and predicts the opponent will do the same. After this patch the AI prices the strike as the self-damage it actually is.

## Why

`trade_value` credits `heal_worth(state, attacker.controller, dealt + splashed + trampled)` whenever a Lifesteal attack lands (`crates/ai/src/reply.rs:169-176`), and `heal_worth` (`crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs:64-72`) never asks whether the heal is replaced. The engine's `healing_replaced` (`crates/engine/src/replacements.rs:546-627`) converts the heal to Pierce damage when a live `HealToDamage` modifier stands on the healed player's opponent — a public R169 badge — or a face-up `heal_to_damage` card acts on the enemy side (`converts_by_text`, `:511-521`). Both are public information the AI may legally read; a still-hidden trap correctly stays unmodeled. The same misprice flows into `ranked_attacks`'s opponent model (`reply.rs:225`) and `even_trade` (`candidates.rs:316-319`). C+ #22 Blood Moon ships the flag (`crates/cards/src/scripts/classic_plus/c022_blood_moon.rs:33`).

## Proposal

In `heal_worth` (or at the call site), replicate the read-only half of `healing_replaced` — live `HealToDamage` modifiers on the healed player's opponents plus face-up `heal_to_damage` acting cards — and price the converted amount as Pierce damage on the healing hero. A test on a Blood Moon board shows the trade's value flipping sign. Run the standard improve screen for an eval change.

## Where it lands

`crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`, `crates/ai/src/reply.rs`, tests under `crates/ai/tests/ai/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Under a live public conversion, a Lifesteal trade's healing term prices self-damage, not healing
- [ ] With no conversion in force, trade values are unchanged
- [ ] A hidden or unrevealed converter changes nothing

## Size and risks

Small: one read-only helper plus a caller tweak and tests, screened per the training pipeline like any eval change.

## Steps

1. In `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`, directly after `heal_worth`, add:
   ```rust
   /// E8, R413: whether a heal of `player`'s hero is replaced by Pierce damage from the
   /// converter, the read-only half of `replacements::healing_replaced`: a live `HealToDamage`
   /// modifier on any other player (R169, both seats see it), or a face-up `heal_to_damage`
   /// card acting on any other player's side (`acting_with_flag`, whose board walk drops
   /// face-down traps per R33/R1487000, so a hidden converter correctly stays unmodeled).
   pub(crate) fn heal_converted(state: &GameState, player: PlayerId) -> bool {
       jackioh_engine::PLAYER_IDS
           .into_iter()
           .filter(|other| *other != player)
           .any(|other| {
               state.players[other].mods.iter().any(|modifier| {
                   matches!(modifier.kind, ModifierKind::HealToDamage { .. })
                       && jackioh_engine::modifier_is_live(state, modifier)
               }) || jackioh_engine::acting_with_flag(state, other, |flags| flags.heal_to_damage)
           })
   }
   ```
   Copy the modifier-iteration shape from `granted_combo_live` in `crates/engine/src/query.rs:462-470` and the flag-reading shape from `emotes_heard` (`query.rs:557-558`). Add `acting_with_flag`, `modifier_is_live`, `PLAYER_IDS` to the existing `use jackioh_engine::{...}` list (all are root re-exports; `ModifierKind` is already imported). Everything read here is public or derived from public board state, so CLAUDE.md rules 4 and 7 hold.
2. In `crates/ai/src/reply.rs`, import the helper: extend line 54's `use crate::evaluate::{...}` with `heal_converted`. Replace lines 169–176 with:
   ```rust
   if lands && has_keyword(&a.view.keywords, KeywordKind::Lifesteal) {
       let amount = on_unit(out.dealt, &t) + splashed + trampled;
       if heal_converted(state, attacker.controller) {
           // E8, R413: the heal becomes that much Pierce damage on the healing hero instead,
           // on the stated amount (`damage.rs`: a replaced heal is never multiplied), ignoring
           // Armor, so `reply_face_value` without `projected_hero_damage`'s Armor pass.
           value -= reply_face_value(state, attacker.controller, amount);
       } else {
           value += heal_worth(state, attacker.controller, amount, &AI_EVAL);
       }
   }
   ```
   Do not touch `even_trade` (`candidates.rs:316-319`) or `ranked_attacks` (line 225): both call `trade_value` and are fixed through it.
3. In `crates/ai/src/reply.rs` `mod tests`, add `use jackioh_engine::{ModifierExpiry, ModifierKind, PlayerModifier};` and three tests following the existing `vanilla_with` + `healed` pattern (constants `VANILLA`, `OOMEN`, `MOON: &str = "classicplus-022"`):
   - `a_lifesteal_hit_under_a_face_up_blood_moon_is_worth_self_damage`: board `p1: {health: 10, field: [VANILLA]}` with Lifesteal granted, `p2: {field: [OOMEN], backrow: [{def: MOON, radiant: true, faceUp: true}]}`; assert `trade.kills` and `trade.value == kill_worth(oomen) - reply_face_value(p1, 4)` (about `3.2 - 4.0 = -0.8`), and that it is below the no-moon baseline from `a_lifesteal_hit_is_worth_the_heal_of_all_it_deals` (about `+6.37`): the sign flips.
   - `a_lifesteal_hit_under_a_live_heal_to_damage_modifier_is_worth_self_damage`: same board without the backrow card, then push `PlayerModifier { id: "moon".into(), expiry: ModifierExpiry::ThisTurn { turn: s.state().turn }, kind: ModifierKind::HealToDamage { converter_id: "moon".into() } }` onto `players[P2]` (the healed hero's opponent); assert the same converted value.
   - `a_hidden_blood_moon_leaves_the_lifesteal_price_unchanged`: same board with `faceUp: false` backrow Moon; assert `trade.value` equals the baseline `kill_worth + healed(10, 4)` exactly.
4. Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --lib reply::tests`, and `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai even_trades`.
5. Run the standard improve screen for an eval change (`training/improve.md`, A screen): build the control from the committed tip (`cargo build --release -p jackioh-tools && cp target/release/jackioh ~/control-jackioh`), make this the only change, then `cargo jackioh arena --a self --b bin:~/control-jackioh --set improve-dev` (400 games); keep the change only if `edgeLow` is above 0, and record the tally in the commit message.

## Tests

- `crates/ai/src/reply.rs`, `mod tests`: `a_lifesteal_hit_under_a_face_up_blood_moon_is_worth_self_damage` asserts exact converted pricing (`kill_worth` less `reply_face_value` for the 4 dealt) and a negative value against the positive baseline.
- Same module: `a_lifesteal_hit_under_a_live_heal_to_damage_modifier_is_worth_self_damage` covers the modifier half of the helper (a fired base-face Moon, which leaves a modifier rather than a face-up card).
- Same module: `a_hidden_blood_moon_leaves_the_lifesteal_price_unchanged` covers the hidden-trap acceptance criterion (face-down text sleeps, R1487000).
- No-conversion behavior is pinned by the existing tests (`a_lifesteal_hit_is_worth_the_heal_of_all_it_deals`, `a_trample_lifesteal_hit_heals_what_lands_on_the_unit_and_on_the_hero`, `a_healing_multiplier_doubles_the_lifesteal_heal_it_prices`, `at_low_life_the_lifesteal_trade_outranks_a_plain_face_hit`), which must pass unmodified.
- Commands: `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --lib reply::tests`, `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai even_trades`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, plus the arena screen above.

## Done when

- [ ] A Lifesteal trade on a live public Blood Moon board prices self-damage (converted test asserts the exact negative value).
- [ ] With no conversion, trade values are unchanged (existing Lifesteal tests pass unmodified).
- [ ] A hidden/unrevealed converter changes nothing (hidden-trap test passes).
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check`, the clippy gate for `jackioh-ai`, the `reply::tests` unit tests, and the `even_trades` integration tests all pass.
- [ ] The 400-game improve-dev screen against a control is recorded, with its edge and interval.

## Risks

- Reading a hidden trap would leak hidden information (rule 7) and misprice: avoided because `acting_with_flag` walks `acting_texts_of`, which filters face-down cards via `lasting_text_dormant`; the hidden-trap test pins this.
- Pricing converted damage with Armor deducted would understate it (Pierce ignores Armor): avoided by using `reply_face_value` directly, not `projected_hero_damage`; the exact-value test pins the unreduced amount.
- Applying the healing multiplier to the converted amount would double-count: avoided because the engine multiplies only heals no replacement took (`damage.rs:1001-1004`); the converted leg uses the stated amount.
- Duos edge: the helper loops all players other than the healed one (mirroring `healing_replaced`'s loop over `active_first` minus the healed player) rather than assuming one opponent.

# #2054: Patch: the AI prices a Lifesteal strike under a public heal-to-damage conversion as the self-damage it is
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When an effect publicly turns healing into damage — say a revealed Blood Moon stands on the board — a Lifesteal attacker's strike hurts its own hero instead of healing it. The practice AI still prices that strike as healing, a bonus with the wrong sign, so it sends its Lifesteal units into boards where they damage their own hero and predicts the opponent will do the same. After this patch the AI prices the strike as the self-damage it actually is.

## Why

`trade_value` credits `heal_worth(state, attacker.controller, dealt + splashed + trampled)` whenever a Lifesteal attack lands (`crates/ai/src/reply.rs:169-176`), and `heal_worth` (`crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs:64-72`) never asks whether the heal is replaced. Both are public information the AI may legally read; a still-hidden trap correctly stays unmodeled. The same misprice flows into `ranked_attacks`'s opponent model (`reply.rs:225`) and `even_trade` (`candidates.rs:316-319`). C+ #22 Blood Moon ships the flag (`crates/cards/src/scripts/classic_plus/c022_blood_moon.rs:33`).

In `heal_worth` (or at the call site), replicate the read-only half of `healing_replaced` — live `HealToDamage` modifiers on the healed player's opponents plus face-up `heal_to_damage` acting cards — and price the converted amount as Pierce damage on the healing hero. A test on a Blood Moon board shows the trade's value flipping sign. Run the standard improve screen for an eval change.

`crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`, `crates/ai/src/reply.rs`, tests under `crates/ai/tests/ai/`.

- [ ] With no conversion in force, trade values are unchanged
- [ ] A hidden or unrevealed converter changes nothing

## Size and risks

Small: one read-only helper plus a caller tweak and tests, screened per the training pipeline like any eval change.

The opponent model (`ranked_attacks`) and `even_trade` inherit the fix through `trade_value` with no edits of their own.

   pub(crate) fn heal_converted(state: &GameState, player: PlayerId) -> bool {

           .filter(|other| *other != player)
